memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now then, divide this land among the nine tribes and half of the tribe of Manasseh." The other half of Manasseh, the Reubenites and the Gadites had received the inheritance that Moses had given them east of the Jordan, as he, the servant of the Lord, had assigned it to them - Josh 13:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Joshua to divide the land among the tribes — but notice something striking. Much of this land had not yet been fully possessed. There were still Philistines and Canaanites in it. And yet God says: divide it now, allocate it as an inheritance. The gift was given even before it was fully enjoyed.

This is how God's promises often work. The inheritance is granted by God's word first, and entered into over time. Israel could begin dividing the land with confidence, not because every enemy was already gone, but because God had promised it to them. His word made it as good as theirs.

The Christian life has this same shape. In Christ, God has already given us every spiritual blessing (Eph 1:3). We are already declared righteous, already adopted, already made heirs. And yet day by day we grow into what is already ours, entering more fully into the reality of what God has granted. We do not strive to earn the inheritance; we live out of an inheritance already secured by Christ's blood. The already-given gift shapes how we live while we wait for its full enjoyment (Rom 8:16-17).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you live as someone who already has an inheritance in Christ, or as someone anxiously trying to earn one?
- What promise of God can you begin trusting even before you fully see it?
- How does knowing your inheritance is secure change how you live today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ my inheritance is already secure. Help me to live confidently out of what You have given, even while I wait to see it fully. Amen.
